title: Enriched inversion commutes with a cartesian parameter
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, Dwyer--Kan equivalences, the model homotopy category $h\mathrm{sCat}$ and the derived pushout localization $q:C\to L_WC$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property]. For small simplicial categories $C,D$, their cartesian product has objects $(c,d)$, mapping sets $C(c,c')\times D(d,d')$, and componentwise composition and identities. Let $W$ be a set of vertex arrows of $C$, and put $W_D=\{(w,1_d):w\in W,\ d\in\operatorname{Ob}D\}$. Then the map $q\times1_D$ induces an isomorphism in $h\mathrm{sCat}$
$$L_{W_D}(C\times D)\longrightarrow (L_WC)\times D.$$
For any representative of this derived comparison it is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. The comparison is natural for enriched functors in both variables preserving the specified arrows. No fibrancy assumption on $C,D$ or saturation assumption on $W$ is imposed; universes contain all the displayed categories.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.14, printed p.896, with cartesian monoidal simplicial sets. Read online 2026-10-17; archival HTT WANTED. No Stacks tag states this homotopical theorem.

proof.text: First note that the localization structure map $q:C\to L_WC$ is essentially surjective on $\pi_0$. Let $Z$ be the full simplicial subcategory of $L_WC$ on the objects $q(c)$, and factor $q=i a$ through its inclusion $i$. The identity of $L_WC$ and the image clause of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property] show that $q$ inverts $W$. Fullness makes $a$ invert $W$ as well: inverses between its objects are still arrows of $Z$. The same universal property gives $v:L_WC\to Z$ in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ with $v q=a$. Its injectivity gives $i v=1$, since both restrict along $q$ to $q$. Applying $\pi_0$ shows that every object of $L_WC$ is isomorphic to an object of $Z$. These statements concern homotopy-category classes, so changing a representative only changes the resulting $\pi_0$ functors by natural isomorphism. This is a few-line application of the cited universal property, not a separate localization lemma.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.14, preparatory essential-image check for the model-target reduction; Notation A.3.5.1 and Proposition A.3.5.5

proof.text: Cartesian product preserves Dwyer--Kan equivalences. Indeed [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] identifies realization of a product of mapping simplicial sets with the product in k-spaces. Paths, maps from spheres and their based homotopies into a product are coordinate pairs, so path components and every homotopy group of a product are products. Thus a weak homotopy equivalence remains one after taking a product with any simplicial set. This also gives $\pi_0(C\times D)=\pi_0C\times\pi_0D$; the product of an equivalence of ordinary categories with an identity is an equivalence by taking the product of its quasi-inverse and unit/counit. Consequently cartesian product descends to $h\mathrm{sCat}$, with no fibrancy requirement. The map $q\times1_D$ sends each $(w,1_d)$ to an isomorphism on $\pi_0$, so [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property] produces a unique comparison class $r:P\to Q$, where $P=L_{W_D}(C\times D)$, $Q=(L_WC)\times D$, and $q':C\times D\to P$, satisfying $r q'=q\times1_D$.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.14, construction of the comparison for cartesian simplicial sets; Proposition A.3.5.5

proof.text: Fix a combinatorial simplicial model category $\mathcal A$ and put $\mathcal B=(\mathcal A^D)^{cf}$. The projective-model assertion of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] makes $\mathcal A^D$ again a combinatorial simplicial model category and makes evaluation of a bifibrant diagram bifibrant. Use [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-exponential] at $I=L_WC$ and at $I=C$. It identifies maps $Q\to\mathcal A^{cf}$ with maps $L_WC\to\mathcal B$, and identifies maps $C\times D\to\mathcal A^{cf}$ with maps $C\to\mathcal B$. Its subset clause identifies the requirement that the latter class invert $W$ in $\pi_0\mathcal B$ with the requirement that its uncurried class invert every arrow in $W_D$ in $\pi_0\mathcal A^{cf}$. This is a condition on whole enriched diagrams: no strict pointwise inverse is chosen.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.14, first and third bijections, using Proposition A.3.4.13 and the projective objectwise weak-equivalence criterion

proof.text:
Write $\operatorname{Hom}_S(U,T)$ for the subset of $\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(U,T)$ whose induced $\pi_0$ functor inverts $S$. The exponential bijections of the previous step and the two applications of [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property] give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(Q,\mathcal A^{cf})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(L_WC,\mathcal B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_W(C,\mathcal B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_D}(C\times D,\mathcal A^{cf})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(P,\mathcal A^{cf}).$$
The middle localization bijection is restriction by $q$, and the last is the inverse of restriction by $q'$. Naturality of enriched evaluation in [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-exponential] says the composite sends $[F]$ to the unique class whose restriction by $q'$ is $[F(q\times1_D)]$. The equation $r q'=q\times1_D$ identifies that class with $[F r]$, by injectivity of $(q')^*$. Thus the displayed bijection is the actual map $r^*$, rather than an unspecified bijection of sets.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.14, four displayed bijections and the final identification of their composite

proof.text: Step 1 makes $q\times1_D$ essentially surjective: for $(x,d)$ choose $c$ with $q(c)$ isomorphic to $x$ and pair that isomorphism with $1_d$. From $r q'=q\times1_D$, every object of $Q$ is therefore isomorphic to an object in the image of $r$. Step 4 proves the bijection on homotopy classes into $\mathcal A^{cf}$ for every combinatorial simplicial model category $\mathcal A$, in universes containing the necessary tests. Both hypotheses of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-target-test] now hold. It gives that $r$ is an isomorphism in $h\mathrm{sCat}$ and that every actual representative of this derived comparison is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence, including representatives made with replacements. Neither $C$ nor $D$ has been assumed fibrant or cofibrant.

source.place: Lemma A.3.5.14, reduction to model-category targets using Lemma A.3.4.6 and Corollary A.3.4.11

proof.text: For enriched functors $f:C\to\widetilde C$, $g:D\to\widetilde D$ with $f(W)\subseteq\widetilde W$, let $\widetilde q$, $\widetilde q'$ and $\widetilde r$ denote the corresponding structure maps and comparison. Functoriality from [lem-coef-simplicial-inversion-universal-property] gives $L(f)$ and $L(f\times g)$. The two sides of the naturality square, $(L(f)\times g)r$ and $\widetilde r L(f\times g)$, have the same restriction by $q'$: both are $(\widetilde q\times1_{\widetilde D})(f\times g)$. Injectivity of $(q')^*$ gives their equality in $h\mathrm{sCat}$. For identities, the induced localization map restricts to $q$, as does the identity; injectivity gives $L(1_C)=1_{L_WC}$. For composable marking-preserving $f_1,f_2$, both $L(f_2)L(f_1)$ and $L(f_2f_1)$ restrict to $q_2f_2f_1$ along $q$, so injectivity gives their equality. These equations and ordinary product functoriality give identity and composition compatibility of the naturality squares. Empty categories and empty markings require no change: products, the inversion condition, and all the displayed bijections retain their usual empty cases.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NW-0b9738db1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read HTT from a local copy left in /tmp by an earlier review (/tmp/q72htt/htt.pdf, 2017 version) and checked A.3.4.6 (p.886), A.3.4.11 (p.889), A.3.4.12-13 (pp.889-890), A.3.5.5 (p.893) and A.3.5.14 (p.896); every printed page cited in the nodes is correct. HTT is still not archived in literature/, so the WANTED line stands. The item is A.3.5.14 for S=sSet with no hypothesis added and nothing weakened; this is not a target node, so no coefficient category or base-change morphism is involved. Step 1: injectivity of restriction along q gives i v=1, so q is essentially surjective on pi0. Step 2: products preserve DK equivalences (via lem-coef-realization-finite-limits), and the universal property gives r with r q'=q x 1. Step 3: the projective model and the new exponential translate the W condition into the W_D condition. Step 4: I traced the composite of the four bijections myself; it is r^*, by naturality of the exponential in I and injectivity of restriction along q'. The universal property is applied with large targets in an enlarged universe, as in HTT. Step 5: pi0(r) is essentially surjective, so the detector applies. Step 6: both sides of the naturality square restrict along q' to the same map, and injectivity gives equality; identities and composition follow the same way. New node lem-coef-simplicial-model-target-test: I proved it from A.3.4.6 and A.3.4.11. Essential surjectivity is genuinely needed for the surjectivity half, and HTT uses it silently. Tested on empty X and Y and on BS^1 -> point. New node lem-coef-simplicial-derived-exponential: it is A.3.4.13 plus a pointwise criterion, which is true because a map of projectively bifibrant diagrams is a weak equivalence exactly when every component is one. Tested with D or I empty and D terminal. Neither new node duplicates an existing one: the existing nodes for A.3.4.11 (lem-coef-simplicial-fully-faithful-homotopy-image) and A.3.4.12 (lem-coef-simplicial-diagram-equivalence-classes) state different results and also reach the item through lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison, so citing them would close a cycle. Neither new node restates a clause of the item. A reachability check on the snapshot found no cycle. All uses are in unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, so no tool_uses are needed. The blueprint fields are correct and no SGA source is used. Advisory: the future splits of the two new nodes must follow HTT's chunk proofs rather than the existing coherent-nerve nodes. No changes made.

lean.statement: theorem simplicial_inversion_product_parameter : ∃ E : ProductDescent.{u}, (∀ (P : Pair.{u}) (D L K : SCat.{u}) (q : P.category ⟶ L) (k : (productPair P D).category ⟶ K), MappingProperty P (bergnerHomotopyFunctor.map q) → MappingProperty (productPair P D) (bergnerHomotopyFunctor.map k) → ProductComparison P D L K q k) ∧ ProductNaturality E
lean.note: Reuses the existing coordinatewise productIndex and productEnrichment definitions, marked Pair, Bergner homotopy category, and MappingProperty. Comparison classes are uniquely fixed by the localization-unit triangle; naturality uses the induced unit triangles and product descent. Representatives include strict functors and three-arrow replacement representatives. No fibrancy or saturation restrictions. The product-owner theorem is not a proof input; its downstream DAG node is not added as a prerequisite.
